title: Two opposite effective line classes on a proper integral algebraic space
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $X$ an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-pc-scheme, def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper, meaning separated, of finite type and universally closed, and $X$ is integral, meaning nonempty, reduced and irreducible. Let $L$ be a line module on its small etale structure sheaf, that is, an $\mathcal O_X$-module etale locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_X$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Write $L^{-1}=\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_X}(L,\mathcal O_X)$, with its local evaluation identification $L\otimes L^{-1}\simeq\mathcal O_X$. If both $\Gamma(X,L)$ and $\Gamma(X,L^{-1})$ contain nonzero sections, then $L\simeq\mathcal O_X$.

proof.text: Choose nonzero $s\in\Gamma(X,L)$ and $t\in\Gamma(X,L^{-1})$. The dual $L^{-1}$ is again a line module: on an etale chart $U$ with $L|_U\simeq\mathcal O_U$ as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], $L^{-1}|_U\simeq\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U,\mathcal O_U)=\mathcal O_U$, and a local basis $e$ of $L$ gives the dual local basis $e^\vee$ of $L^{-1}$ with $e^\vee(e)=1$. Properness includes separatedness and finite type, so [lem-sfb-space-generic-line-section-injectivity] applies to $M=L$ and to $M=L^{-1}$. At a geometric generic point $\bar\eta$ its injectivity makes both germs $s_{\bar\eta}$, $t_{\bar\eta}$ nonzero. Its field stalk $F$ makes $L_{\bar\eta}$ a one-dimensional vector space; taking $e$ on a trivializing chart through which $\bar\eta$ factors, $s_{\bar\eta}=a e$ and $t_{\bar\eta}=b e^\vee$ with $a,b\in F\setminus\{0\}$, so the germ of the evaluation $c=t(s)\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ is $ab\ne0$. Consequently $c$ is nonzero, since the germ of a zero section is zero.

An irreducible nonempty point space is connected: a disconnection would express it as the union of two proper closed subsets. Thus $X$ is proper, reduced, nonempty and connected, exactly the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-space-proper-connected-function-field]. This gives a field $K=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Since $c\ne0$, choose its multiplicative inverse $d=c^{-1}\in K$. There is no claim that $K=k$, and no geometric connectedness assumption is used.

The section $s$ defines $u:\mathcal O_X\to L$, and $v=d\,t:L\to\mathcal O_X$ is a sheaf-module morphism. On every etale chart trivializing $L$ as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], write $s=a e$, $t=b e^\vee$. The two maps have coefficients $a$ and $db$, and both composites have coefficient $dab=dc=1$. Hence $vu=1$ and $uv=1$ on the charts and therefore on the sheaves, by uniqueness in the sheaf axiom. Thus $u$ and $v$ are inverse isomorphisms, proving $L\simeq\mathcal O_X$.
